clue.text: Might the solution be cracked by uncles and kings?

definitions.text: Might the solution be cracked by uncles and kings?

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king, and the plural asks for two of them

explanation.surface: A riddle wondering whether some puzzle could be broken open by a gang of uncles and kings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters crack into the answer, and the answer is something people famously crack.
explanation.definitionFit: People crack their finger joints, so those joints are exactly the thing that might be cracked.

clue.text: Tax Gordon Brown, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old word for a levy or payment
second meaning: a person from Scotland, as the former Chancellor and Prime Minister is

explanation.surface: A call to impose a levy on the Chancellor of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was Chancellor of the Exchequer in 2002, so taxing reads naturally with his name; here he is simply an example of a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The old levy survives in 'scot-free', and Brown, born in Scotland, is an example of its natives.

clue.text: Very verily

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as an intensifier, as in very good
second meaning: truly, in all honesty

explanation.walkthrough: Two near-identical words that each mean the same short adverb in different uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb works as an intensifier like 'extremely' and as an assertion of truth like 'truly'.

clue.text: Normally solver and setter nonchalant about being topless

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
something topless has lost its top, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: a nonchalant manner is casual
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: A comment that, as ever, the solver and setter are relaxed about going shirtless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solver and setter' is you and me, a common crossword way of asking for the pronoun covering both.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something normally is doing it the way one customarily does it.

clue.text: Spurs' nightmare — a fragile defence?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two words: the cockerel is the Spurs emblem, and a hell full of eggs would be its bad dream
second meaning: the thin casing protecting a developing chick

explanation.surface: A football fan bemoaning the club's brittle back line.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur ('Spurs') is a London football club whose badge is a cockerel; split the answer as EGGS HELL for its nightmare.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin calcium casing protecting a developing bird is a famously breakable kind of protection.

clue.text: Make alterations to restore ICI item of furniture

indicators.note: making alterations changes the arrangement, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; ICI was a big British chemicals company

explanation.surface: An instruction to modify something so as to bring a chemical company back to health.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a writing desk with drawers and a hinged flap, a classic piece of antique furniture.

clue.text: Who, say, is Spike?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the title character of the BBC science-fiction series ... Who
second meaning: to tamper with, as in adding something to a drink

explanation.surface: A question asking which person is called Spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' looks like a question word, but it is the Time Lord of the long-running BBC series.
explanation.definitionFit: The Time Lord is known simply by his title, and to adulterate a drink or a report is to tamper with it.

clue.text: Underwear — darn it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: women's or girls' pants
second meaning: a mild British exclamation of annoyance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Darn' looks like mending clothes, which suits underwear, but it is the euphemistic curse; in Britain 'knickers!' is used the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names women's pants and also serves as a mild British expletive of irritation.

clue.text: Enthusiasm shown for Guardian leader on "Guardian Unlimited"

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundary letters, so both ends are cut off
the leader is the one in front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the newspaper's name
custos is Latin for a keeper or guardian, found in English dictionaries

explanation.surface: Praise for the newspaper's editorial appearing on its old website, Guardian Unlimited.
explanation.walkthrough: Guardian Unlimited was the Guardian's website; here the second Guardian is CUSTOS with its ends removed, set after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with zest and relish is doing it with keen enthusiasm.

clue.text: Back-to-front musical jazz improvisation

indicators.note: taking the back of the word and putting it at the front moves its final letter to the start

parts.note: Andrew Lloyd Webber's long-running stage show

explanation.surface: A description of jazz improvising done backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-to-front' tempts a full reversal (STAC), but only the last letter moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing nonsense syllables in place of words is the vocal improvising style of jazz singers.

clue.text: Aristophanes play where satyr's tail's turned

indicators.note: something turned has been twisted round, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A Greek comedy in which a goat-legged satyr's tail gets twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 's after tail is 'is', joining wordplay to the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Greek comic dramatist's famous comedy in which women withhold sex to end a war.

clue.text: Appropriate capital for New York? I'd lay a pound on it!

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a fitting choice of capital city for the state

definitions.text: I'd lay a pound on it!
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the state capital that is apt because it literally ends in the state's abbreviation NY; the setter bets on it

explanation.surface: A confident bet on which city ought to be New York State's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is apt because its last two letters are the state's postal abbreviation; the exclamation is just the setter's wager.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hudson River city is the seat of government of New York State, and finishes with its postal code.

clue.text: One supporter stands for Judas, but not one judge

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading upward, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: but not one says a single numeral one is taken out of the word

parts.note: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus and is the archetypal betrayer

explanation.surface: Someone who backs a case stands up for Judas, though no one else judges him.
explanation.walkthrough: IBRA reads upward to ARBI; TRAITOR then loses its I, the 'one', to give TRATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbitrator is appointed to settle a dispute, acting as an adjudicator between the parties.

clue.text: A fresh flower is opening

parts.note: taken as written
pert means cheeky or saucy, a sense of fresh
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure runs through Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A newly opened bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom but means a river, here the Ure in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole or gap, such as a camera's lens hole, is an opening.

clue.text: Line on map is round West Country city

parts.note: taken as written
the round letter O
Bath is a Somerset spa city in the West Country, south-west England

explanation.surface: A cartographer's line drawn around a city in the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is round' looks like a container instruction, but the pieces simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a contour line on a chart joining points of equal water depth.

clue.text: Not hard to afford the new, compromised exchange

indicators.note: making something new reworks it, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not hard says the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils, is taken out

parts.note: H for hard, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: Easily able to pay for the latest thing in a deal involving concessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not hard' reads as 'easy' in the surface; here it removes the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal where each side gives up something to gain something else is a balanced swap made by conceding.

clue.text: Curvy figure sounds like a kissing couple

indicators.note: sounds like tells the solver to say the phrase out loud and listen to it

parts.note: a couple locked in a kiss are all lips

explanation.surface: A shapely person who resembles a pair of smoochers.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is the geometric shape whose curve is closed and symmetrical, a curved figure.

clue.text: Breaking up is super!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: British slang for terrific or excellent

explanation.surface: A cheerful claim that ending a relationship is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking up' suggests a split between partners, but it means shattering.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means shattering things to bits, and in British speech it is also an enthusiastic word for wonderful.

clue.text: Warehouse area's moral oxymoron?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the section of a warehouse where deliveries are received
second meaning: a virtuous transgression is a self-contradiction

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a storage depot can contain a contradiction in ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the phrase becomes GOOD SIN, a contradiction in moral terms; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliveries arrive at the receiving bay of a store, which is labelled with this phrase.

clue.text: Endless bearer of gifts demanding Shakespearean villain's capital

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: Father Christmas brings presents
the schemer in Othello

explanation.surface: A tireless gift-giver insisting on the wicked Iago's chief city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakespearean villain's capital' looks like one phrase, but the 's is 'is' and capital stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chilean seat of government is a principal city, an example of a nation's capital.

clue.text: Able to tune radio set at last

indicators.note: to tune is to adjust, so these letters are adjusted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of set

explanation.surface: Finally managing to tune in a wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilful and dexterous is capable and clever with their hands.

clue.text: Part of a boot to step around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A section of footwear used for walking about.
explanation.definitionFit: The reinforced covering over the front of a boot protects the wearer's toes.

clue.text: Temporary home providing shelter for an occupant

indicators.note: something that shelters something else has it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a tent is a short-term dwelling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A makeshift dwelling sheltering someone who lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rents and lives in a property is its resident.

clue.text: "_______ outta here!" It's war!

parts.note: the blank is filled by a drawled 'I'm a-gettin' outta here', a well-known pun

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing in a hurry because fighting has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no indicator: the fill-in-the-blank only works if the word is said in a cowboy drawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the final great battle at the end of the world, so any catastrophic conflict.

clue.text: Eric Bristow speaks of the game behind which he stood

parts.note: the speaker whose Cockney accent shapes the sound: he drops his aitches

indicators.note: speaks of points to how the word sounds in the darts player's own London accent

parts.note: the stick-and-ball game, said with the initial H dropped

explanation.surface: A darts champion reminiscing about his sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Bristow was a five-time world darts champion with a broad London Cockney accent, so hockey comes out without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A darts player throws from behind this marked line on the floor, so it is where Bristow stood.

clue.text: Bond given part in "Othello", a thankless task

indicators.note: part in says the word is a portion sitting inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the play's name and into the next words
surface padding completing the phrase about an unrewarding job

explanation.surface: James Bond cast in a Shakespeare tragedy, an unrewarding job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy, but it means a binding promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn sworn promise binds the person who makes it, like a bond.

clue.text: "Home and Away" is a diversion going to pot

parts.note: at home means in
away means off, as in off work

explanation.surface: A dig that the Australian soap Home and Away is a pastime going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards or snooker an in-off is a ball that goes into a pocket after glancing off another, so a diverted ball 'going to pot'.
explanation.definitionFit: The shot sends a ball deflected off another ball into a pocket, being diverted on its way there.

clue.text: Setting off for an odd double gin and it

indicators.note: something odd is strange or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a double measure is two gins
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ordering a strange gin and Italian vermouth, with a double gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and it is a British cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting a fuse or firework is setting it off by kindling it.
